content.text:
Numbers are now rounded only when shown: at most 10 significant digits, no trailing zeros, and exponent form only at 1e10 and above or below 1e-9. What you type shows exactly as typed. `data-value` holds the exact value. Dividing by zero (with `=` or a chained operator) shows `Error` and `data-error="true"`, and only clear works until pressed. I ran the examples in a quick Node harness and all passed; not tested in a browser.

I removed the old `toPrecision(15)` in `compute`, because it rounded stored values. So `0.1 + 0.2 =` still shows `0.3`, but `data-value` is now `0.30000000000000004`. In the error state `data-value` is `NaN`, since you didn't specify it.

I rejected keeping any rounding in stored values, because it builds up through chained calculations.
